_comment: F-13: source of truth for what each sandbox image's build is pinned to - base image digest, key direct-dependency versions, and any per-image dependency lockfile. docker/check_images_lock.py verifies this file stays in sync with the Dockerfiles (run in CI, see .github/workflows/ci.yml's dockerfile-lint job). Regenerate the 'base_digest' fields by hand after a deliberate `docker buildx imagetools inspect <tag>` refresh - this file does not auto-update, it's a checked assertion of what the Dockerfiles currently declare.

known_gaps: apt packages (build-essential, python3, nodejs, npm, sqlite3, curl, unzip) install from the live Debian archive at build time with no snapshot.debian.org pin - deferred, not a 'clear fix': would require repointing apt sources to a dated snapshot mirror and accepting that mirror's availability/rate limits.

no committed go.sum, but this is by design and not the same gap as pyyaml/npm/cargo: `go get <pkg>@<exact version>` at build time resolves the full transitive graph once into the shared module cache, and GOPROXY=off + GOSUMDB=off (set for check_command time) mean nothing can re-resolve against a different upstream state afterward - the cache itself is the lock. A go.sum on disk would be redundant with no drift it actually prevents.

Maven resolves the warmup pom.xml's full dependency-tree versions (managed by spring-boot-starter-parent, tracked above) against Maven Central at build time with no dependency-tree lockfile equivalent to package-lock.json/Cargo.lock - Maven's ecosystem has no first-class lockfile mechanism analogous to npm/cargo, so the top-level parent version is what's tracked here, not every transitive version it resolves to.

NuGet restore against offline.nuget.config resolves warmup.csproj's already-version-pinned PackageReferences with no packages.lock.json committed - `dotnet restore --use-lock-file` would generate one; deferred here since it requires a .NET toolchain to regenerate and wasn't independently verified against this image's exact restore graph.

composer itself installs via the upstream installer script (signature-verified against composer.github.io/installer.sig, not floating-tag risk in the H-03 sense) - no case-facing composer.json/composer.lock exists yet to lock.
gem installs (minitest, rake) are version-pinned in the Dockerfile directly; no Gemfile/Gemfile.lock exists since there's no transitive gem graph to lock at this image's current size.
